Where it began

Mustafizur Rahman was born on 6 September 1995 in Satkhira, a small town in Khulna, Bangladesh. As a boy he played tennis-ball cricket, and he played it as a batsman. His hero was the Pakistan pace bowler Mohammad Amir.

Scouts first spotted him at an Under-17 tournament in his home town. In 2012 he went to Dhaka to try out for a camp for fast bowlers, and the Bangladesh Cricket Board took him into its fast-bowling programme. In 2014 he went to the Under-19 World Cup in the UAE, where he took eight wickets, and he made his first-class debut for Khulna Division the same year.

The player

His first game for Bangladesh was a T20 against Pakistan in April 2015. That June came his first one-day internationals, against India. He took five wickets in the first game and six in the second, and nobody had taken more in his first two ODIs. Bangladesh won the series.

His Test debut followed in 2015, against South Africa, and he took four wickets in the series. He played 15 Tests between 2015 and 2022, taking 31 wickets at 36.74 with a best of four for 37. In the shorter games he became a fixture. He was Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker at the 2019 World Cup, with 20 in eight matches, and in 2016 he became the first Bangladeshi to take five wickets in a T20 World Cup match.

What made him special

His great weapon was the off-cutter: a slower ball that moved away from the right-hander. He has said it began when his team-mate Anamul Haque urged him to try a slower delivery. Batsmen found it very hard to read. In May 2025 he became the first bowler to send down 300 dot balls in the final overs of T20 internationals.

His batting was a gentler matter. The tennis-ball batsman of his youth made 66 runs in 22 Test innings, with a top score of 16. On the evidence, switching ends was a wise move.

Away from the middle

He is known as The Fizz, a nickname from the 2015 Bangladesh Premier League, where his cutters first caught the eye. In 2016 he was named the ICC's Emerging Cricketer of the Year, the first Bangladeshi to win one of its annual awards. The same year he was the IPL's Emerging Player as Sunrisers Hyderabad won the title, the first overseas player to receive it.

The ICC picked him in its ODI Team of the Year in 2015, 2018 and 2021, and in its T20I team in 2021. He also played for Sussex in England and for several IPL sides, and during the 2024–25 season he became only the fourth bowler to take 100 wickets in the Bangladesh Premier League.

And finally

It is a nice twist that he started out as a batsman. In his tennis-ball days in Satkhira, Mustafizur was the one with the bat in his hand. The rest of the cricket world was only too glad he changed his mind.
